new.title: Cross the red bridge in Leverkusen's Japanese Garden
new.desc: Tucked into the Carl-Duisberg-Park beside the Bayer works, this garden was first laid out in 1912 for the chemical magnate Carl Duisberg. Koi and turtles drift under the red Mikado bridge, which copies one in Nikko, next to a little tea house.
new.tip: It is a short walk from Leverkusen-Mitte station; come in spring or when the maples turn in autumn, when the reflections in the ponds are at their best.

new.title: See modern art in Schloss Morsbroich, Leverkusen
new.desc: A moated Rococo palace, once a commandery of the Teutonic Order, has housed Leverkusen's museum of modern art since 1951 and was named German Museum of the Year in 2009. Op Art, kinetic and monochrome works fill rooms built for courtly life.
new.tip: Leave time for the landscape park around the moat: its sculptures and small waterfall are free to wander, and a signed trail follows the Dhuenn from here.

new.title: Hear the hammers at the Freudenthaler Sensenhammer
new.desc: This scythe factory in Leverkusen-Schlebusch worked until 1987 and is now an industrial museum, with the forges, workers' houses and owner's villa still grouped around the hall. On demonstration days the old water-driven hammers thunder back to life.
new.tip: Combine it with the flat riverside walk along the Dhuenn to Schloss Morsbroich; you pass the old weir that once fed the hammers.

new.title: Have cake on the Wupper at Waldhaus Roemer, Opladen
new.desc: A half-timbered house right on the banks of the Wupper, where locals stop for homemade cake and coffee after a riverside walk. It is one of the few places in Leverkusen that still lays on a full Bergische Kaffeetafel.
new.tip: The Kaffeetafel needs pre-ordering for groups; on Sundays and holidays come early for the breakfast.

new.title: Refuel with pancakes at Haus Ferger, Schlebusch
new.desc: A pancake house on the old Bergische Landstrasse in Leverkusen-Schlebusch, a classic stop for hikers coming down the Dhuenn valley. Thick Rhineland Pfannkuchen, sweet or savoury, are the whole point.
new.tip: It sits near the end of the Dhuenn trail from the Sensenhammer, so save your appetite for after the walk.

new.title: Climb Balthasar Neumann's staircase in Schloss Augustusburg, Bruehl
new.desc: The prince-archbishops of Cologne built this Rococo palace and the nearby hunting lodge Falkenlust, a UNESCO World Heritage pair since 1984. The marble, jasper and stucco staircase by Balthasar Neumann is the showstopper.
new.tip: The baroque garden with its fountains and mirror pool is free; walk the lime alley through the park to Falkenlust. Bruehl station is right opposite the palace.

new.title: Ride Taron through Klugheim at Phantasialand, Bruehl
new.desc: Germany's most densely themed theme park has been squeezing rides into a small plot in Bruehl since 1967. In the rock village of Klugheim the multi-launch coaster Taron weaves between basalt cliffs, and F.L.Y. sends you face down over steampunk Rookburgh.
new.tip: Head straight to the big coasters at opening time; queues build fast by late morning, especially on weekends.

new.title: Visit Abtei Brauweiler, Pulheim
new.desc: Founded in 1024, this Benedictine abbey's Romanesque church of St. Nikolaus towers over the flat fields west of Cologne. Its later life as workhouse and Gestapo prison, where Konrad Adenauer was held in 1944, is told at a memorial on the site.
new.tip: On summer evenings the cloister hosts open-air classical concerts; the abbey park around it is lovely for a stroll at any time.

new.title: Stare into the Hambach mine from Forum :terra nova, Elsdorf
new.desc: At the edge of one of Europe's largest open-cast lignite mines, this viewpoint lets you look down into a man-made canyon with giant bucket-wheel excavators. The building's facade copies the coloured earth layers dug out below.
new.tip: There is coffee and a snack inside; cyclists can arrive on the Speedway :terra nova path along the old conveyor belt route.

new.title: Swim at the Otto-Maigler-See beach, Huerth
new.desc: A former lignite pit filled with groundwater is now Cologne's favourite lake beach, with about half a kilometre of fine sand on the north shore. Swans and ducks winter on the rest of the lake, which is a nature reserve.
new.tip: Swimming is only allowed inside the paid Strandbad; bus 711 stops right at the lake.

new.title: Treat yourself at Schloss Loersfeld, Kerpen
new.desc: A moated castle first mentioned in 1262, set in a ten-hectare English landscape park between two forests, with a restaurant counted among Germany's finest. It is the rare fine-dining address you reach in hiking boots.
new.tip: Book ahead, then walk off lunch on the easy 11 km loop from the castle to the Boisdorfer See and its nature reserves.

new.title: Eat asparagus or Reibekuchen at the Hallerhof, Bergheim
new.desc: This farm restaurant on the edge of the Koenigsdorfer Forst, a woodland planted on old mining land, is famous for its own asparagus. Thursday is Reibekuchen day, when the Rhineland potato pancakes take over the menu.
new.tip: In spring the farm shop sells freshly cut asparagus; the beer garden and playground make it easy with kids.

new.title: Drink Franconian beer at the Waldbiergarten Liblar, Erftstadt
new.desc: A forest beer garden near the Liblarer See that cheerfully ignores Koelsch and pours Engel beer from Franconia instead: Helles, Kellerbier and Bock. Hearty plates like Kaesspaetzle and beer goulash come to your table.
new.tip: It is only 400 m from Erftstadt station, outdoor seats only, cash only, and open from Easter into autumn.

new.title: Step inside Zumthor's Bruder-Klaus-Feldkapelle, Mechernich
new.desc: A local farming couple asked Peter Zumthor for a chapel in their field near Wachendorf. He stacked 112 spruce trunks into a tepee, poured rammed concrete around them and then burned the wood out, leaving a charred, dark interior open to the sky.
new.tip: Park on Iversheimer Strasse and walk the last half kilometre through the fields; it is closed on Mondays and quietest early in the day.

new.title: Stand under the Effelsberg radio telescope, Bad Muenstereifel
new.desc: Hidden in a wooded Eifel valley, this 100 m dish was the largest fully steerable radio telescope on Earth for almost three decades. Seeing the 3,200 tonne structure tilt above the trees is surreal.
new.tip: Walk in on the planet trail from Effelsberg village: it scales the solar system down and ends at a model of the Sun beside the visitor pavilion.

new.title: Walk the town walls of Bad Muenstereifel
new.desc: The Erft runs straight through this Eifel spa town, still ringed by an almost complete medieval wall with 18 towers and four gates. Inside, the shops of an outlet centre hide in half-timbered houses, and the Romanisches Haus from 1167 is one of the oldest stone houses in the region.
new.tip: Parts of the wall walk are open; start at the Orchheimer Tor and the RB 23 from Euskirchen stops just outside the walls.

new.title: Face the past at Vogelsang, Schleiden
new.desc: The Nazis built this hilltop complex above the Urftsee in the 1930s to train party cadres; after the war it served Belgian troops until 2005. Today it is a sobering place of remembrance and a gateway to the Eifel National Park.
new.tip: Allow time for the exhibition, then follow one of the trails down into the national park for views over the lake.

new.title: Leave an apple at Kloster Steinfeld, Kall
new.desc: One of Germany's earliest vaulted churches crowns a hill in the Eifel, with a Baroque Koenig organ from 1727 among the finest in the Rhineland. Pilgrims place fresh apples on the tomb of Hermann Joseph, the abbey's beloved saint.
new.tip: The monastery now runs a guest house and art academy, so you can stay overnight; check the church calendar for organ concerts.

new.title: Explore the Roman baths of Zuelpich
new.desc: Under a modern museum in Zuelpich lie the remains of a 2nd century Roman bath house, used for almost 200 years. The Museum der Badekultur then follows bathing habits from medieval bathhouses to modern spas.
new.tip: Follow the 18-station outdoor trail around the excavation, and check the calendar for the monthly public tour.

new.title: Find the source of Cologne's Roman water at Gruener Puetz, Nettersheim
new.desc: At this spring in the Urft valley the Romans tapped water for Cologne, sending it some 95 km downhill by gravity alone through the longest aqueduct north of the Alps. The reconstructed spring house marks the start of the Roemerkanal-Wanderweg.
new.tip: Follow the first stage of the trail from Nettersheim station; information boards point out where original channel sections surface.

new.title: Cheer the knights at Burg Satzvey, Mechernich
new.desc: Often called the best-preserved original moated castle in the Rhineland, Satzvey has staged knight tournaments since 1981. Jousts at Pentecost and in late summer, Walpurgis night and an Advent castle Christmas market fill the year.
new.tip: Take the RB 24 to Satzvey station and walk 600 m; the outside of the castle is free to see on any day.

new.title: Watch eagles fly at the Wildgehege Hellenthal
new.desc: This 65-hectare wildlife park on the edge of the Eifel National Park shows lynx, wildcats, wild boar and red deer, but the stars are in the raptor station. Eagles, kites, falcons and even an Andean condor take to the air in daily flight shows.
new.tip: Plan your visit around the flight demonstrations; the park is open all year and has its own restaurant for a break.

new.title: Breakfast at the Krewelshof farm cafe, Mechernich
new.desc: A pond-side farm in Obergartzem whose own bakery supplies the cafe with breads and cakes, from a farm-produce breakfast buffet to seasonal lunches. Every autumn it turns into NRW's biggest pumpkin show, with over 100,000 pumpkins carved into giant sculptures.
new.tip: Visit between September and early November to see the pumpkin show; try the pumpkin seed bread from the farm bakery.

new.title: Look up at the west window of the Altenberger Dom, Odenthal
new.desc: Cistercian monks began this Gothic abbey church in a quiet Dhuenn valley in 1259. Most windows are plain grey grisaille as their order required, which makes the huge coloured west window from around 1400 glow all the more; Catholics and Protestants have shared the church since the 1850s.
new.tip: Come in the late afternoon when the sun hits the west window from outside; organ concerts are held here regularly.

new.title: Sit down to a Bergische Kaffeetafel at the Kuechenhof, Altenberg
new.desc: The Bergische Kaffeetafel is a feast of coffee from a pewter Droeppelmina, rice pudding on currant bread, waffles with hot cherries and cream, then black bread with curd cheese. The Kuechenhof, right beside the Altenberger Dom, serves it every afternoon.
new.tip: Arrive between 14:30 and 17:30 and come hungry; the Kaffeetafel traditionally ends with a small schnapps.

new.title: Watch the dancing fountains in the Maerchenwald Altenberg
new.desc: Since 1931 a family has run this woodland trail of 18 Grimm fairy tales, from Rapunzel to Rumpelstilzchen, with scenes that move and talk. In the hall at the end, coloured fountains from 1956 dance to classical music, still worked by hand.
new.tip: Pair it with the Altenberger Dom just down the hill and a walk along the Dhuenn.

new.title: Spot the 'Aapefelse' at Bensberg town hall, Bergisch Gladbach
new.desc: Gottfried Boehm wrapped the ruins of a 12th century hilltop castle in raw concrete to create this town hall in 1962 to 1972. The jagged stair tower so baffled residents that they nicknamed it the Aapefelse, the monkey rock.
new.tip: The courtyard is open to walk through; look for the old five-sided keep that Boehm kept inside the new ring.

new.title: Taste farm cheese at the Thomashof, Burscheid
new.desc: A farm with its own dairy on the edge of the forest above the Eifgenbach valley, making cheese and milk products for its shop and farm cafe. The breakfast buffet with fresh dairy and homemade jam is a local weekend ritual.
new.tip: Walk off breakfast on the loop into the Eifgenbach valley to the old Rausmuehle mill, about an hour and a half each way.

new.title: Have cake in the forest at Waldcafe Steinhaus, Bergisch Gladbach
new.desc: On the edge of the Koenigsforst, an old forester's lodge and barn house a visitor centre and a small forest cafe serving homemade cakes. It is the classic reward after a walk through the woods and heath of the nature reserve.
new.tip: From the Technologie-Park bus stop it is a short walk over the A4 footbridge; the cafe is open Thursday to Sunday.

new.title: Cycle the Balkantrasse through Burscheid and Wermelskirchen
new.desc: The old railway nicknamed the Balkan Express is now a 50 km cycle path with gentle gradients, running from Leverkusen-Opladen through Burscheid and Wermelskirchen into the Bergisch hills. Old railway milestones and converted stations line the way.
new.tip: Start at Opladen station so you climb gently on the way out and coast back; the converted station building in Burscheid makes a good halfway stop.
